title: exFAT write preparation becomes stale before copy/publication
mechanism: ExfatInode::write_at computes new_size and resizes the page cache under inner.write(), releases the lock, copies under a fresh upread() where Vmo::write silently clamps to the current capacity, then publishes the stale new_size and returns the full count. A competing extending write or truncate in the gap shrinks the cache or overtakes the size.
contract: write(2): a successful write returns the bytes actually stored, and after it returns the file size covers the written range and reads return the written data.
observed: Two racing extending pwrite64 calls on one exFAT file: one returned 4096 after storing 0 bytes and left st_size beyond the cache (reads return 4096 without data), or st_size regressed below an already-successful write.
fix_refs: /home/chin39/Documents/asterinas-dev branch fix/exfat-write-size-race: 864356cec (Hold the exfat inode lock across a buffered write), 3ece54702 (fs/write_race test), base upstream/main bc12195df

repro.how_to_run: Preferred: apply write_race-regression.patch and run the fs regression suite with SMP>=2. The /exfat case fails on an unfixed tree. Exact 01b schedules: apply mc3-l3-timing-hook.patch to the pin, build guest_mc3.c with -DMC3_MODE=3 (CE order) or -DMC3_MODE=4 (regression order), boot with -smp 2 and an exFAT disk.
repro.runtime_status: REPRODUCED at 604948581 with a Level 3 timing hook (01b MC-3, SMP=2). The write_race regression fails 65 to 93 of 2000 rounds at bc12195df (SMP=4)

caveats: 01b reproduction needed a Level 3 timing-only kernel hook (500 hook-free trials at the pin did not trigger). Hook-free regression evidence is at bc12195df, not the pin. Fixed-tree A/B covers the writers shape. Both exact 01b schedules still need a retest. The fix leaves AST-15 open. handoff-01b.md still cites the older series (d5b645d84 + 97199dd30, 79/2000). The register's 864356cec/3ece54702 (65 to 93/2000) is followed here.
